stem: How did a voter cast a vote in the first general election?
options: Dropped a blank ballot paper into the chosen candidate's box
Put a stamp on the chosen candidate's name on a ballot paper
Pressed a button against the chosen candidate on a machine
Wrote the chosen candidate's name on a printed ballot paper

stem: Which sequence correctly shows how the method of voting in Indian general elections changed over time?
options: Stamped ballot paper, then separate candidate boxes, then EVM
EVM, then separate candidate boxes, then stamped ballot paper
Separate candidate boxes, then EVM, then stamped ballot paper

stem:

stem: Read the passage on votes and seats in the 1952 Lok Sabha election. Which feature of the electoral system best explains the gap between the Congress's vote share and its seat share?
options: The candidate with most votes wins the seat, even without a majority
Seats are shared among parties in proportion to their vote share
Only parties crossing a fixed share of votes can win any seats
The Prime Minister is directly elected, which boosts their party
explanation: Correct option: (A). Under the first-past-the-post system, the candidate with more votes than any other wins, so the party that leads in votes tends to get much more than its proportional share. The non-Congress vote was divided among rival candidates, so 45 per cent of votes gave the Congress about 74 per cent of seats. Option (B) describes proportional representation, India has no vote threshold for seats, and the Prime Minister is not directly elected.

stem: When the Congress was formed in 1885, what kind of organisation was it?
options: A mass movement of peasants and rural workers
A pressure group of the newly educated and professional classes
A revolutionary party seeking armed overthrow of British rule

explanation: Correct option: (B). stem: Why has the first decade of electoral competition in India been described as the 'Congress system'?
options: The Constitution gave the Congress a special legal status
Opposition parties were not allowed to contest until the 1960s
The Congress acted both as the ruling party and the opposition

explanation: Correct option: (C). Because factions within the Congress took different ideological positions and competed with each other, political competition took place within the Congress itself.
